content: Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of vincristine by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of vinorelbine by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of zaleplon by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ziprasidone by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of zolpidem by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of zonisamide by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of abemaciclib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers reduces plasma concentrations of abemaciclib and its metabolites. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of abiraterone by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, increase abiraterone dosage frequency from once daily to twice daily. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A inducer is necessary, increase the acalabrutinib dose to 200 mg twice daily. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of acebutolol by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of acetaminophen by increasing its metabolism, potentially enhancing the production of hepatotoxic metabolites. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of acetaminophen IV and rectal formulations by increasing metabolism, potentially enhancing the production of hepatotoxic metabolites. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Phenobarbital and acetazolamide may synergistically increase the risk of anticonvulsant-induced osteomalacia. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of albuterol by increasing sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of alfentanil by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of alfuzosin by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of almotriptan by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of alosetron by altering hepatic enzymes CYP1A2, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of alpelisib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of alprazolam by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of alvimopan by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ambrisentan by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of amikacin by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of amiodarone by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and amisulpride both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of amitriptyline by altering hepatic enzymes CYP2C19, CYP3A4, and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs increase sedation. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of amlodipine by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and amobarbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and amoxapine both increase sedation. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital increases metabolism and reduces blood concentrations of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), potentially increasing adverse effects, including respiratory depression, at toxic doses. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while amphetamine decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of amphotericin B deoxycholate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III by increasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of apalutamide by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or substitute another drug when possible. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of apixaban by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Phenobarbital and apomorphine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of apremilast by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of aprepitant by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while arformoterol decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. Phenobarbital reduces the effects of argatroban by increasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of aripiprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of armodafinil by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of artesunate by increasing metabolism, potentially decreasing the active metabolite (DHA). Monitor for decreased efficacy. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of ascorbic acid by increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Phenobarbital and asenapine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of atazanavir by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of atenolol by increasing metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during co-administration. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of atogepant by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of atorvastatin by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the effects of atracurium by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of avanafil by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of avapritinib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of avatrombopag by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely.
